findings.note: Checkpoint validity is central to resume safety, but the spec defers exact evidence rules and does not give observable criteria for deciding when completion evidence or relevant changes invalidate a checkpoint. The interruption scenarios therefore lack a stable pass/fail classification for valid versus stale/invalid evidence; define a contract-level validity rule or an explicit fail-closed outcome.

The criteria quantify results across ?every? or ?the? portable scenario set, but the set has no minimum inventory or coverage boundary. Since the outcomes depend on scenario selection, a small or selectively scoped set could satisfy the percentages while missing specified edge cases. Tie each criterion to a bounded set derived from the listed acceptance scenarios and edge cases.

These checked items assert all requirements are testable, success criteria measurable, and every FR covered. That overstates the artifacts: checkpoint-validity classification is deferred to planning and the success-criteria scenario denominator is not bounded. Reassess these checks after the corresponding spec gaps are resolved.
